cells.tense: The work is finished, or nearly, and the finishing feels right — you're here with it, pen still in hand.
cells.ask: Put one more thing into this current — a single move that rides the momentum you already have, not a fresh start from a stop.
cells.core:
You bring things to a close, and you can feel when they're closed — not because every piece is perfect but because what you pictured has been lived all the way through. That felt sense is the signal, and it's saying this part is done and the next part wants to begin. Let the ending open something instead of shutting a door: the settled feeling is a place to rest, not a place to stop.

One more offering into the same current is what keeps this alive — the drive and the feeling pointing the same way, nothing forced and nothing stalled. What you get for it is forward motion that doesn't have to be pushed.
cells.sheetLine: You finish what you make, and you can feel when it's done — start the next one from that settled place.
cells.verb: Fulfillment — imagining something all the way through until it is fully felt and complete.
cells.place: the point where what has been made is gathered whole and then let go into what comes next.

cells.tense: You're bracing toward a version of this that hasn't arrived yet — living ahead of where the work actually is.
cells.ask: Choose one thing already growing and tend it exactly as it is — water what's there before you plant anything new.
cells.core:
You're reaching past where the work actually sits, trying to force the next shape before the current one has finished being itself. The future is being held open with both hands, gripped so tightly that nothing can arrive on its own — and the ending, the part you wanted, can't come while you're squeezing ahead of it. The push to arrive is what's costing you the arrival.

Tend what's already on the ground and let it grow at its own rate, and tending it won't drain you. Hold the space without clutching, and you'll be handed a completion that lands without being forced.
cells.sheetLine: You're forcing the next version before this one is finished — tend what's already growing and let it arrive.

cells.tense: You finished something real, and you're still standing where you set it down — the door behind you, not in front.
cells.ask: Say one true thing you already know about the work — quietly, once, before you're certain it deserves saying.
cells.core:
There's a made thing behind you and you haven't picked it back up — the picture that ran all the way through and landed, the satisfaction that was already yours. You stopped before you called it done, and stopping has turned into standing still. Nothing was taken from you. The only thing absent is your own permission to know what you know without proof first.

One honest word about the work — the thing you'd say if nobody were checking — puts the current back into the part that's run dry. You'll be handed a knowing that lands without argument, and a floor under the next thing you make.
cells.sheetLine: You finished something and haven't claimed it — say what you already know, before you're sure it's worth saying.

cells.tense: The pen is still moving — you are already writing this, and you're talking about it as if someone else were holding it.
cells.ask: Notice one part of the work you've been calling its own course, and say to yourself, once, that you were the one who pictured it there.
cells.core:
You're already imagining the next step into being — in the choices you make, the things you keep, the order you put them in — but you describe it as if the work were arriving under its own steam. The making is happening. The knowing that you're the maker isn't. The ending is right there, waiting for you to say it's yours.

Attention that refines instead of worries, solitude that connects instead of isolates — that is how the recognition becomes real without turning into strain. You'll be handed a vision you can trust because you know where it came from.
cells.sheetLine: You're already shaping what comes next — say it's you doing it, and the finish will feel like yours.
